answer: An answer must cite at least 3 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. Because the river index resolves every citation against the pigment checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the pearl audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 128 aliases hence pays the authoring cost 128 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 14 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
